newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT STILL IN TALKS ON PAPER PARTNERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT STILL IN TALKS ON PAPER PARTNERSHIP.

text.p: Dutch paper and office equipment group Koninklijke KNP BT said on Thursday it was still looking for a strategic partner for its paper unit KNP Leykam.
"At the moment we are working hard on several options and we are in talks with a number of interested parties," chief financial officer Rob Bonnier told a news conference.

He declined to give further information on the number of possible partners, their identities or the form which a cooperation pact might take but added that KNP BT still planned to make an announcement about this subject before the end of this year.
KNP BT said last year it was seeking a strategic partnership for its paper production division.
Market sources later mentioned several international firms which were said to be interested in teaming up with KNP Leykam, including Sweden's Stora and Finland's Enso Gutzeit .
But both companies and KNP BT itself repeatedly declined to comment on the rumours,
Earlier today, KNP BT said its Leykam unit had a 22 million guilder operating profit in the first half of 1997, compared with an operating loss of 24 million in the year-ago period.
In the second quarter of this year the paper division had an operating profit of 14 million guilders, up from a loss of 17 million in the same period of 1996.

KNP Leykam's return on investment (ROI) was a meagre 2.2 percent in the second quarter, up from a negative 3.2 percent in the year-ago period but still way below the ROI goal of 15 percent or more that KNP BT has set for itself and its units.
Bonnier said KNP Leykam's current reorganisation should improve its performance, which should enable the division to reach the profitability levels set by its parent company.
"But that will take a few more years," he added.
KNP BT's two other divisions, distribution and packaging, performed in line with the company's goals with second quarter ROI levels of 15.6 and 16.9 percent respectively.
Due to the ailing paper division, the group's total return on investment was 10.3 percent in the second quarter of this year, up from eight percent in the second quarter of 1996.
Bonnier said the group's performance should improve in the years ahead through the reorganisations at KNP Leykam and KNP Packaging and because of gains from recent investments.
